↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). COLOSSAE or Colosse, a city of Phrygia, on the Lycus, which is a tributary of the Maeander. It does not appear that Paul had visited this city when he wrote his letter to the church there (Colossians 1:2). ↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). EPAPHRAS lovely, spoken of by Paul (Colossians 1:7; 4:12) as “his dear fellow-servant,” and “a faithful minister of Christ.” He was thus evidently with him at Rome when he wrote to the Colossians. He was a distinguished disciple, and probably the founder of the Colossian church. ↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos II.62-64 (c. 350 AD)

'Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature' — Athanasius marks eikōn tou theou tou aoratou (image of-the invisible-God) as the perfect-image confession (the Father, invisible, has his perfect-visibility in the Son-eikōn). The prōtotokos pasēs ktiseōs (firstborn of-all-creation) is the Arian-controversy verse-pair to Pr 8:22. Athanasius's interpretation: prōtotokos (firstborn) is NOT a created-priority (which would require ek-tisis-language; cf. Ps 89:27 LXX-prōtotokos of David's-anointing-as-king) but an economic-headship over the creation the Son agentially-effects (Col 1:16 en autō ektisthē ta panta — 'in him all things were created'). The Son is firstborn-OVER-creation (genitive of subordination), not firstborn-IN-creation. Tewahedo Christological-headship theology cites Col 1:15-18 as the cosmic-Headship-triad.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos II.62 (c. 350 AD)

'For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him' — Athanasius marks en autō ektisthē ta panta (in-him all-things were-created) as the Pauline-creator-Christology summit. If 'all things' (ta panta) were created in/through/for the Son, then the Son is NOT himself among-the-all-things (otherwise self-creation would be required); the Son is therefore-uncreated. Athanasius reads Col 1:16 + Jn 1:3 (panta di' autou egeneto — 'all things were made through him') as the canonical-Pauline-Johannine creator-Christology pair, fielding the Arian objection at its strongest point. Tewahedo cosmological-theology cites Col 1:16 at every Anaphora's institution-prefatory cosmic-acknowledgment.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos II.63 (c. 350 AD)

'And he is before all things, and by him all things consist' — Athanasius marks autos estin pro pantōn kai ta panta en autō synestēken (he is before all things and in him all things consist/hold-together) as the Pauline-cosmic-sustainer-Christology. The synestēken (hold-together, cohere) is a PRESENT-CONTINUOUS-cosmic-act, not a past-creation event. Christ is not merely-the-Creator (Col 1:16 past-act) but the ongoing-cosmic-Sustainer (Col 1:17 present-state). If the Word were-not, the cosmos would cease-to-cohere. Tewahedo cosmological-doxology cites Col 1:17 + Heb 1:3 (pherōn ta panta) as the cosmic-Christ-sustainer pair.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos II.63 (c. 350 AD)

'And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence' — Athanasius marks the dual-prōtotokos: Col 1:15 prōtotokos pasēs ktiseōs (firstborn of all creation = pre-eminent creator) AND Col 1:18 prōtotokos ek tōn nekrōn (firstborn from the dead = pre-eminent resurrection). The same Word-incarnate is firstborn-over-creation AND firstborn-from-the-dead — bookending the entire-economy with prōtotokos-headship. The kephalē-of-the-body-ecclesiology grounds the Church-as-Christ's-body in the Christological-head-membership relation. Tewahedo ecclesiology cites Col 1:18 + Eph 1:22-23 as the head-body-ecclesiological pair.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.6 (c. 350 AD)

'For it pleased the Father that in him should all fulness dwell' — Athanasius marks pan to plērōma katoikēsai (the whole fullness dwell) as a SECOND-articulation of Col 2:9 (pan to plērōma tēs theotētos sōmatikōs — paired in γ.4.9 seed). Col 1:19 emphasizes the Father's-pleasure as the ground (eudokēsen — was-well-pleased) of the divine-fullness-dwelling-bodily. The incarnation is not accidental but eternally-intended-by-the-Father; the Son's-kenotic-assumption is the Father's-eternal-will being realized. Tewahedo Christmas (Lǝdat) doxological reading cites Col 1:19 + Mt 3:17 (Father's-voice 'in whom I am well-pleased') as the eudokia-incarnational pair.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.34 (c. 350 AD)

'For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily' — Athanasius marks pan to plērōma tēs theotētos sōmatikōs (all the fulness of-the Godhead bodily) as the unsurpassable Pauline-incarnation-confession. The plērōma (fulness) is not partial (against any subordinationist diminution); it is pan to plērōma (ALL the fulness). The theotētos (of-Godhead — abstract-noun naming the divine-nature-itself, not theiotēs which would name divinity-as-attribute) is the highest-possible divine-predication. The sōmatikōs (bodily) names the genuine-embodied-human mode of the divine-fulness's dwelling. The verse therefore names: ALL the very-divine-essence dwells BODILY in the incarnate-Christ. Tewahedo Christological-confession cites Col 2:9 (paired with Heb 1:3) at every Christmas (Lǝdat) + Theophany (Tǝmqät) acclamation.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §25 (c. 350 AD)

'Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross' — Athanasius marks exaleipsas to kath' hēmōn cheirographon (blotting out the handwriting against us) prosēlōsas auto tō staurō (nailing it to the cross) as the Pauline-cross-as-receipt-cancellation anchor. The cheirographon (handwritten bond — the IOU of human-transgression-against-divine-law) is publicly-cancelled by being-nailed to the cross itself. The verse exegetes the cross's soteriological-mechanism in legal-financial language. Tewahedo Holy-Friday cross-meditation cites Col 2:14-15 as the cheirographon-cancellation paschal-anchor.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §54 (c. 350 AD)

'When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory' — Athanasius marks ho Christos hē zōē hymōn (Christ, the life of-yours) as the THEŌSIS-ESCHATOLOGICAL-SUMMIT anchor: Christ IS the believer's-life-itself (not merely-the-source-of-life). When-he-appears (phanerōthē — eschatological-manifestation), believers-appear-with-him-in-glory — the theōsis-grant fulfilled at the eschaton. Athanasius's signature formula 'He was made man that we might be made God' (DI §54) reaches its temporal-completion at the Col 3:4 phanerōsis. The Tewahedo Easter-vigil hymnody cites Col 3:4 as the saint-glorified-with-Christ Paschal-fulfillment.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.40 (c. 350 AD)

'Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus' — Athanasius marks touto phroneite en hymin ho kai en Christō Iēsou (this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus) as the PARAENETIC-DOORWAY into the Phil 2:6-11 hymn. The kenotic-Christology of vv. 6-11 is not a stand-alone-treatise but an exhortation-to-imitation grounded in Christology. The believer's-life is shaped-by the Word's-kenotic-pattern: descent-then-exaltation, self-emptying-before-glory. Tewahedo monastic-formation reads Phil 2:5-11 at every novice's clothing-rite as the kenotic-vocation-anchor.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.40 (c. 350 AD)

'Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God' — Athanasius marks en morphē theou hyparchōn (subsisting-in the form-of-God) as the eternal-divine-pre-incarnation state of the Son. The hyparchōn (subsisting — strong ontological present-participle, NOT a temporary-state-verb) names the eternally-possessed-divine-form. The to einai isa theō (the-being equal-with-God) is what the Son already-had and did-not-cling-to (ouch harpagmon hēgēsato — did-not-consider-rapine, did-not-grasp-to-himself). The Arian-reading that would make morphē-theou a creaturely-honor-given-to-a-creaturely-Son cannot accommodate the hyparchōn-present-tense or the isa-theō-equality-with-God; the verse positively-requires eternal-pre-incarnation divinity. Tewahedo Christmas-and-Holy-Friday hymnody pairs Phi 2:6 with 2 Cor 8:9 + Heb 1:3 as the kenosis-anchor-triad.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.41-45 (c. 350 AD)

'But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men' — Athanasius marks heauton ekenōsen (he-emptied-himself) as the kenotic-act that is NOT a subtraction-of-divine-attributes but an ASSUMPTION-of-human-attributes. The eternal-Word remained morphē-theou-subsisting (Phi 2:6) AND took morphēn doulou-labōn (the form of a servant). The kenosis is the incarnation; the incarnation is the kenosis. The morphēn-doulou-labōn (form-of-servant taking) is what makes the en homoiōmati anthrōpōn genomenos (in-the-likeness-of-men becoming) possible — the divine-Word voluntarily-assumes the servant-form so that the incarnate-life can be lived in genuine-human-mode. Tewahedo Christological-kenotic-theology preserves the Athanasian-reading exactly: kenosis-is-assumption, NEVER subtraction.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §22 (c. 350 AD)

'And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross' — Athanasius marks ginomenos hypēkoos mechri thanatou, thanatou de staurou (becoming obedient unto death, even death of the cross) as the kenotic-trajectory-summit. The two-mechri (unto / even) escalations name the uttermost-depth of the descent: not merely-incarnation, not merely-death, but specifically the CRUCIFORM-death (the Roman-shameful-execution mode). The cross is therefore both the Christological-summit of obedience AND the soteriological-summit of redemption. Tewahedo cross-veneration (the Mäskäl Feast September 27) cites Phil 2:8 as the kenotic-obedience-of-the-cross anchor.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.41-45 (c. 350 AD)

'Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name' — Athanasius marks dio kai ho theos auton hyperhypsōsen (wherefore-also God highly-exalted-him) as the post-resurrection enthronement-corollary of the kenotic-descent. The Arian-reading would make this an ontological-promotion (a created-Son rewarded with divine-status); Athanasius refutes this by tracing the verse's continuity-of-Subject: the SAME Son who eternally-subsisted in morphē-theou (Phi 2:6) and voluntarily-took morphē-doulou (Phi 2:7-8) is the SAME Son hyper-hypsōthēnai (highly-exalted, Phi 2:9). The exaltation is therefore not a promotion-to-divinity (which the Son already-possessed) but a public-revelation-of-divinity in the now-incarnate-mode. Tewahedo Easter (Fāsika) liturgy pairs Phi 2:9-11 with Mt 28:18 + Acts 2:36 + Heb 1:3-4 as the exaltation-fourfold.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.42 (c. 350 AD)

'That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth' — Athanasius marks pan gony kampsē epouraniōn kai epigeiōn kai katachthoniōn (every-knee bow of heavenly + earthly + under-earthly) as the UNIVERSAL-ACKNOWLEDGMENT-of-divine-lordship. The three-tiered cosmography (heavens above + earth + Sheol-below) is exhausted by the en-Iēsou-onomati (in-name-of-Jesus) homage. The verse echoes Isa 45:23 (every-knee-bow before YHWH) — the Pauline-citation transfers the YHWH-prerogative explicitly to the incarnate-Jesus-name. Tewahedo Anaphora preserves Phil 2:10-11 + Isa 45:23 as the universal-knee-bow Christological-acclamation.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §54 (c. 350 AD)

'Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body, according to the working whereby he is able even to subdue all things unto himself' — Athanasius marks metaschēmatisei to sōma tēs tapeinōseōs hēmōn symmorphon tō sōmati tēs doxēs autou (transform the body of our humility conformable to the body of his glory) as the eschatological-theosis Pauline-anchor. The transformation is BODILY (not merely-spiritual), into-the-pattern-of Christ's resurrection-glorified-body. This is the FINAL-stage of the Athanasian theosis-arc that began with the incarnation. Tewahedo eschatological-resurrection-doctrine cites Phil 3:21 + 1 Cor 15:51-52 + 1 Jn 3:2 as the bodily-resurrection-glorification triadic-anchor.

'That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him' — Athanasius marks anakephalaiōsasthai ta panta en tō Christō (to-recapitulate all-things in Christ) as the cosmic-scope-of-the-incarnation: the Word's-becoming-man does not merely save individual-souls but RECAPITULATES the entire created-order in himself. The ana-kephalaiōsis (re-heading) restores Christ as the cosmic-Head-over-all-things that the original creation-order required (Col 1:18 head-of-the-body) and that the Fall fragmented. The Tewahedo cosmic-liturgical-theology (the Praises of Christ as cosmic-recapitulator at every Anaphora's anaphoric-section) preserves Eph 1:10's recapitulation-doctrine as constitutive of the entire liturgical-cosmic-restoration.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.42 (c. 350 AD)

'Far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come' — Athanasius marks hyperanō pasēs archēs (far-above every principality) as the exaltation-supremacy Pauline-anchor paired with Phil 2:9 (highly-exalted). The Christ-incarnate-and-risen is RANKED-ABOVE every conceivable angelic or human authority — in BOTH this-age AND the-age-to-come (eschatological-permanence). Tewahedo angelology preserves this Pauline-supremacy-of-Christ at the Christ-Pantocrator iconography of every Tewahedo-dome.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §16 (c. 350 AD)

'For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us' — Athanasius marks autos gar estin hē eirēnē hēmōn (he himself is our peace) as the Pauline-incarnational-peace-anchor. Christ does not merely-make-peace; he IS peace (predicate-identity, like 1 Cor 1:30). The both-made-one names Jew-Gentile-reconciliation but the deeper-anchor is human-divine-reconciliation: the Word's-incarnate-Person IS the union-of-the-two-natures, making him constitutively-peace between God and humanity. Tewahedo Aksumite-Gentile-mission theology cites Eph 2:14-18 at the Frumentius-mission anchor.

'One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all' — Athanasius marks the SEVENFOLD-HENOTĒS (heis Kyrios + mia pistis + hen baptisma + heis theos kai Patēr pantōn) as the TRINITARIAN-MONOTHEISM Pauline-synthesis. The seven 'ones' do not flatten the Trinitarian-distinctions but articulate the divine-unity-in-Trinity: one-Lord (the Son), one-baptism (in the Trinity per Mt 28:19), one-Spirit (implied; cf. Eph 4:4 above), one-God-and-Father — the Three are the unique-one-God. The eph' hēmin pantōn (above all, through all, in you all) names the Father's universal-divine-presence operating through the Son and in the Spirit.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.46 (c. 350 AD)

'(Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?)' — Athanasius marks katebē eis ta katōtera merē tēs gēs (descended into the lower parts of the earth) as the Pauline-affirmation of the descent-into-hades / harrowing-of-Sheol. The Word-incarnate's death was not merely-physical-cessation but ACTIVE-descent into Sheol-of-the-dead to extract the captive-righteous (1 Pet 3:19 paired). The katō / anō (below/above) pairing of Eph 4:9-10 names the cosmic-rescue-arc the incarnation accomplishes. Tewahedo Holy-Saturday (Qǝddus-Sǝnbät) preserves the descent-into-Sheol kerygma explicitly via Eph 4:9-10 + 1 Pet 3:19 + Acts 2:24 in the office of the descent.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.46 (c. 350 AD)

'He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things' — Athanasius marks ho katabas autos estin kai ho anabas (the one who descended is the same as the one who ascended) as the IDENTITY-of-PERSON-across-the-paschal-mystery. The descent into death AND the ascent above-all-heavens are predicated of the SAME Subject (the incarnate-Word) without internal-duality. The hina plērōsē ta panta (that he might fill all things) names the cosmic-pleroma-fulfillment Christ accomplishes. Tewahedo Ascension (Ǝrgät) liturgy cites Eph 4:9-10 as the descent-ascent-cosmic-pleroma triadic kerygma.

TYCHICUS chance, an Asiatic Christian, a “faithful minister in the Lord” (Ephesians 6:21, 22), who, with Trophimus, accompanied Paul on a part of his journey from Macedonia to Jerusalem (Acts 20:4). He is alluded to also in Colossians 4:7, Titus 3:12, and 2 Timothy 4:12 as having been with Paul at Rome, whence he sent him to Ephesus, probably for the purpose of building up and encouraging the church there. ↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §25 (c. 350 AD)

'Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree' — Athanasius marks genomenos hyper hēmōn katara (having become for-us a curse) as the Pauline-substitutionary-summit. The Word-incarnate VOLUNTARILY-takes-on the legal-cursed-status (per Deut 21:23 quoted) that human-disobedience earned — and ABSORBS-it-in-his-own-flesh on the cross. The katara (curse) is taken-into-the-divine-Person and exhausted-by-his-resurrection-acceptance. Tewahedo Holy-Friday liturgical-meditation cites Gal 3:13 + Deut 21:23 + 1 Pet 2:24 as the cursed-on-the-tree triple-anchor.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos II.31 (c. 350 AD)

'Now a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one' — Athanasius marks ho de mesitēs henos ouk estin / ho de theos heis estin (the mediator is not of one / but God is one) as the Pauline-monotheism + Christological-mediation conjunction. The verse preserves divine-unity (theos heis estin — God-is-one, the Shema Pauline-formulation) AND establishes Christ's-mediatorial-office (mesitēs between God and humanity, requiring two-natures: divine to represent God + human to represent humanity). Tewahedo Christological-summary cites Gal 3:20 + 1 Tim 2:5 as the mediator-of-two-natures Pauline-pair.

↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.30 (c. 350 AD)

'But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law' — Athanasius marks genomenon ek gynaikos (made-of-woman) as the genuine-human-birth confession that excludes every Docetic-phantasm reading. The Son is not merely-clothed-in-flesh, not merely-passing-through-Mary-as-a-channel — he is genomenon ek gynaikos in the same mode every human-being is born of woman. The genomenon ek / genomenon hypo combination (born-of-woman + born-under-the-law) names the dual-conformity-to-humanity that the incarnation achieves: biologically-human + legally-human. The Tewahedo Wǝddāse-Maryam preserves Gal 4:4 as the Marian-incarnational summit alongside Lk 1:38 + Mt 1:23 + Isa 7:14 as the four-fold Theotokos-witness.

Of the Godhead bodily dwelling in Christ (Colossians 2:9), i.e., the whole nature and attributes of God are in Christ. (4.) ↩ ◇ Athanasius of Alexandria (350). Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.48 (c. 350 AD)

'And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father' — Athanasius marks to pneuma tou huiou autou (the Spirit of his Son) as the pneumatological-anchor of theosis-by-adoption. The Spirit-of-the-Son-by-nature creates sonship-by-grace in the believer; the SAME Spirit who cried 'Abba' in the incarnate-Son's-Gethsemane (Mk 14:36) now cries 'Abba' in the adopted-believer. The intra-divine Filial-Spirit-Father-relation becomes the believer's-divine-relation by participation. Tewahedo baptismal-chrismation rubric cites Gal 4:6 + Rom 8:15 + Mk 14:36 as the Abba-adoption-Spirit triadic anchor.

'The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all. Amen' — Athanasius marks the triadic Pauline-benediction as the closing-Trinitarian-doxology of Paul's most-personal letter. The three-fold structure (grace-of-Christ + love-of-God + koinonia-of-Spirit) names each Person by his characteristic economic-action: Christ's-grace = the redemption; God's-love = the Father's-sending-of-the-Son; Spirit's-koinonia = the church's-life-in-the-divine-fellowship. Tewahedo liturgical-benediction-formulae (recited at every dismissal) preserve 2 Cor 13:14's three-fold-structure as the Trinitarian-blessing-anchor.

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 11:1.

Would to God ye could bear with me a little in [my] folly: and indeed bear with me.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ὄφελον ἀνείχεσθέ μου μικρὸν τῇ ἀφροσύνῃ· ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀνέχεσθέ μου.

Douay-Rheims

Would to God you could bear with some little of my folly: but do bear with me.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Utinam sustineretis modicum quid insipientiæ meæ, sed et supportare me:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لَيْتَكُمْ تَحْتَمِلُونَ غَبَاوَتِي قَلِيلًا! بَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُحْتَمِلِيَّ.

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 11:2.

For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present [you as] a chaste virgin to Christ.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ζηλῶ γὰρ ὑμᾶς θεοῦ ζήλῳ· ἡρμοσάμην γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἑνὶ ἀνδρὶ παρθένον ἁγνὴν παραστῆσαι τῷ χριστῷ.

Douay-Rheims

For I am jealous of you with the jealousy of God. For I have espoused you to one husband that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

æmulor enim vos Dei æmulatione. Despondi enim vos uni viro, virginem castam exhibere Christo.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

فَإِنِّي أَغَارُ عَلَيْكُمْ غَيْرَةَ ٱللهِ، لِأَنِّي خَطَبْتُكُمْ لِرَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ، لِأُقَدِّمَ عَذْرَاءَ عَفِيفَةً لِلْمَسِيحِ.

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 11:3.

But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Φοβοῦμαι δὲ μήπως ὡς ὁ ὄφις Εὔαν ἐξηπάτησεν ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτοῦ, οὕτως φθαρῇ τὰ νοήματα ὑμῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἁπλότητος τῆς εἰς τὸν χριστόν.

Douay-Rheims

But I fear lest, as the serpent seduced Eve by his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted, and fall from the simplicity that is in Christ.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Timeo autem ne sicut serpens Hevam seduxit astutia sua, ita corrumpantur sensus vestri, et excidant a simplicitate, quæ est in Christo.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَلَكِنَّنِي أَخَافُ أَنَّهُ كَمَا خَدَعَتِ ٱلْحَيَّةُ حَوَّاءَ بِمَكْرِهَا، هَكَذَا تُفْسَدُ أَذْهَانُكُمْ عَنِ ٱلْبَسَاطَةِ ٱلَّتِي فِي ٱلْمَسِيحِ.

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 11:4.

For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we have not preached, or [if] ye receive another spirit, which ye have not received, or another gospel, which ye have not accepted, ye might well bear with [him].

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Εἰ μὲν γὰρ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἄλλον Ἰησοῦν κηρύσσει ὃν οὐκ ἐκηρύξαμεν, ἢ πνεῦμα ἕτερον λαμβάνετε ὃ οὐκ ἐλάβετε, ἢ εὐαγγέλιον ἕτερον ὃ οὐκ ἐδέξασθε, καλῶς ἠνείχεσθε.

Douay-Rheims

For if he that cometh preacheth another Christ, whom we have not preached; or if you receive another Spirit, whom you have not received; or another gospel which you have not received; you might well bear with him.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Nam si is qui venit, alium Christum prædicat, quem non prædicavimus, aut alium spiritum accipitis, quem non accepistis: aut aliud Evangelium, quod non recepistis: recte pateremini.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

فَإِنَّهُ إِنْ كَانَ ٱلْآتِي يَكْرِزُ بِيَسُوعَ آخَرَ لَمْ نَكْرِزْ بِهِ، أَوْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْخُذُونَ رُوحًا آخَرَ لَمْ تَأْخُذُوهُ، أَوْ إِنْجِيلًا آخَرَ لَمْ تَقْبَلُوهُ، فَحَسَنًا كُنْتُمْ تَحْتَمِلُونَ!

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنِّي أَحْسِبُ أَنِّي لَمْ أَنْقُصْ شَيْئًا عَنْ فَائِقِي ٱلرُّسُلِ.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 11:9.

And when I was present with you, and wanted, I was chargeable to no man: for that which was lacking to me the brethren which came from Macedonia supplied: and in all [things] I have kept myself from being burdensome unto you, and [so] will I keep [myself].

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

καὶ παρὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑστερηθείς, οὐ κατενάρκησα οὐδενός· τὸ γὰρ ὑστέρημά μου προσανεπλήρωσαν οἱ ἀδελφοί, ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας· καὶ ἐν παντὶ ἀβαρῆ ὑμῖν ἐμαυτὸν ἐτήρησα καὶ τηρήσω.

Douay-Rheims

And, when I was present with you, and wanted, I was chargeable to no man: for that which was wanting to me, the brethren supplied who came from Macedonia; and in all things I have kept myself from being burthensome to you, and so I will keep myself.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Et cum essem apud vos, et egerem, nulli onerosus fui: nam quod mihi deerat, suppleverunt fratres, qui venerunt a Macedonia: et in omnibus sine onere me vobis servavi, et servabo.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّ ٱحْتِيَاجِي سَدَّهُ ٱلْإِخْوَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ أَتَوْا مِنْ مَكِدُونِيَّةَ. وَفِي كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَفِظْتُ نَفْسِي غَيْرَ ثَقِيلٍ عَلَيْكُمْ، وَسَأَحْفَظُهَا.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 11:22.

Are they Hebrews? so [am] I. Are they Israelites? so [am] I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so [am] I.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἑβραῖοί εἰσιν; Κἀγώ. Ἰσραηλῖταί εἰσιν; Κἀγώ. Σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ εἰσιν; Κἀγώ.

Douay-Rheims

They are Hebrews: so am I. They are Israelites: so am I. They are the seed of Abraham: so am I.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Hebræi sunt, et ego: Israëlitæ sunt, et ego: semen Abrahæ sunt, et ego.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

أَهُمْ عِبْرَانِيُّونَ؟ فَأَنَا أَيْضًا. أَهُمْ إِسْرَائِيلِيُّونَ؟ فَأَنَا أَيْضًا. أَهُمْ نَسْلُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ؟ فَأَنَا أَيْضًا.

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 11:23.

Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I [am] more; in labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Διάκονοι χριστοῦ εἰσιν;- παραφρονῶν λαλῶ- Ὑπὲρ ἐγώ. Ἐν κόποις περισσοτέρως, ἐν πληγαῖς ὑπερβαλλόντως, ἐν φυλακαῖς περισσοτέρως, ἐν θανάτοις πολλάκις,

Douay-Rheims

They are the ministers of Christ (I speak as one less wise). I am more; in many more labours, in prisons more frequently, in stripes above measure, in deaths often.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Ministri Christi sunt (ut minus sapiens dico), plus ego: in laboribus plurimis, in carceribus abundantius, in plagis supra modum, in mortibus frequenter.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

أَهُمْ خُدَّامُ ٱلْمَسِيحِ؟ أَقُولُ كَمُخْتَلِّ ٱلْعَقْلِ، فَأَنَا أَفْضَلُ: فِي ٱلْأَتْعَابِ أَكْثَرُ، فِي ٱلضَّرَبَاتِ أَوْفَرُ، فِي ٱلسُّجُونِ أَكْثَرُ، فِي ٱلْمِيتَاتِ مِرَارًا كَثِيرَةً.

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

in itineribus sæpe, periculis fluminum, periculis latronum, periculis ex genere, periculis ex gentibus, periculis in civitate, periculis in solitudine, periculis in mari, periculis in falsis fratribus:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بِأَسْفَارٍ مِرَارًا كَثِيرَةً، بِأَخْطَارِ سُيُولٍ، بِأَخْطَارِ لُصُوصٍ، بِأَخْطَارٍ مِنْ جِنْسِي، بِأَخْطَارٍ مِنَ ٱلْأُمَمِ، بِأَخْطَارٍ فِي ٱلْمَدِينَةِ، بِأَخْطَارٍ فِي ٱلْبَرِّيَّةِ، بِأَخْطَارٍ فِي ٱلْبَحْرِ، بِأَخْطَارٍ مِنْ إِخْوَةٍ كَذَبَةٍ.

Douay-Rheims

Arabic (Van Dyck)

I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Οἶδα ἄνθρωπον ἐν χριστῷ πρὸ ἐτῶν δεκατεσσάρων- εἴτε ἐν σώματι οὐκ οἶδα· εἴτε ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματος οὐκ οἶδα· ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν- ἁρπαγέντα τὸν τοιοῦτον ἕως τρίτου οὐρανοῦ.

أَعْرِفُ إِنْسَانًا فِي ٱلْمَسِيحِ قَبْلَ أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً. أَفِي ٱلْجَسَدِ؟ لَسْتُ أَعْلَمُ، أَمْ خَارِجَ ٱلْجَسَدِ؟ لَسْتُ أَعْلَمُ. ٱللهُ يَعْلَمُ. ٱخْتُطِفَ هَذَا إِلَى ٱلسَّمَاءِ ٱلثَّالِثَةِ.

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 12:6.

For though I would desire to glory, I shall not be a fool; for I will say the truth: but [now] I forbear, lest any man should think of me above that which he seeth me [to be], or [that] he heareth of me.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

ἐὰν γὰρ θελήσω καυχήσασθαι, οὐκ ἔσομαι ἄφρων· ἀλήθειαν γὰρ ἐρῶ· φείδομαι δέ, μή τις εἰς ἐμὲ λογίσηται ὑπὲρ ὃ βλέπει με, ἢ ἀκούει τι ἐξ ἐμοῦ.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

فَإِنِّي إِنْ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَفْتَخِرَ لَا أَكُونُ غَبِيًّا، لِأَنِّي أَقُولُ ٱلْحَقَّ. وَلَكِنِّي أَتَحَاشَى لِئَلَّا يَظُنَّ أَحَدٌ مِنْ جِهَتِي فَوْقَ مَا يَرَانِي أَوْ يَسْمَعُ مِنِّي.

And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Καὶ εἴρηκέν μοι, Ἀρκεῖ σοι ἡ χάρις μου· ἡ γὰρ δύναμίς μου ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ τελειοῦται. Ἥδιστα οὖν μᾶλλον καυχήσομαι ἐν ταῖς ἀσθενείαις μου, ἵνα ἐπισκηνώσῃ ἐπ’ ἐμὲ ἡ δύναμις τοῦ χριστοῦ.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ’s sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Διὸ εὐδοκῶ ἐν ἀσθενείαις, ἐν ὕβρεσιν, ἐν ἀνάγκαις, ἐν διωγμοῖς, ἐν στενοχωρίαις, ὑπὲρ χριστοῦ· ὅταν γὰρ ἀσθενῶ, τότε δυνατός εἰμι.

Douay-Rheims

For which cause I please myself in my infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ. For when I am weak, then am I powerful.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Propter quod placeo mihi in infirmitatibus meis, in contumeliis, in necessitatibus, in persecutionibus, in angustiis pro Christo: cum enim infirmor, tunc potens sum.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِذَلِكَ أُسَرُّ بِٱلضَّعَفَاتِ وَٱلشَّتَائِمِ وَٱلضَّرُورَاتِ وَٱلِٱضْطِهَادَاتِ وَٱلضِّيقَاتِ لِأَجْلِ ٱلْمَسِيحِ. لِأَنِّي حِينَمَا أَنَا ضَعِيفٌ فَحِينَئِذٍ أَنَا قَوِيٌّ.

↩

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 12:11.

I am become a fool in glorying; ye have compelled me: for I ought to have been commended of you: for in nothing am I behind the very chiefest apostles, though I be nothing.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Γέγονα ἄφρων καυχώμενος· ὑμεῖς με ἠναγκάσατε· ἐγὼ γὰρ ὤφειλον ὑφ’ ὑμῶν συνίστασθαι· οὐδὲν γὰρ ὑστέρησα τῶν ὑπὲρ λίαν ἀποστόλων, εἰ καὶ οὐδέν εἰμι.

Douay-Rheims

I am become foolish: you have compelled me. For I ought to have been commended by you: for I have no way come short of them that are above measure apostles, although I be nothing.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Factus sum insipiens, vos me coëgistis. Ego enim a vobis debui commendari: nihil enim minus fui ab iis, qui sunt supra modum Apostoli: tametsi nihil sum:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

قَدْ صِرْتُ غَبِيًّا وَأَنَا أَفْتَخِرُ. أَنْتُمْ أَلْزَمْتُمُونِي! لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ أُمْدَحَ مِنْكُمْ، إِذْ لَمْ أَنْقُصْ شَيْئًا عَنْ فَائِقِي ٱلرُّسُلِ، وَإِنْ كُنْتُ لَسْتُ شَيْئًا.

↩

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 12:12.

Truly the signs of an apostle were wrought among you in all patience, in signs, and wonders, and mighty deeds.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Τὰ μὲν σημεῖα τοῦ ἀποστόλου κατειργάσθη ἐν ὑμῖν ἐν πάσῃ ὑπομονῇ, ἐν σημείοις καὶ τέρασιν καὶ δυνάμεσιν.

Douay-Rheims

Yet the signs of my apostleship have been wrought on you, in all patience, in signs, and wonders, and mighty deeds.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

signa tamen apostolatus mei facta sunt super vos in omni patientia, in signis, et prodigiis, et virtutibus.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

إِنَّ عَلَامَاتِ ٱلرَّسُولِ صُنِعَتْ بَيْنَكُمْ فِي كُلِّ صَبْرٍ، بِآيَاتٍ وَعَجَائِبَ وَقُوَّاتٍ.

↩

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 12:13.

For what is it wherein ye were inferior to other churches, except [it be] that I myself was not burdensome to you? forgive me this wrong.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Τί γάρ ἐστιν ὃ ἡττήθητε ὑπὲρ τὰς λοιπὰς ἐκκλησίας, εἰ μὴ ὅτι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ οὐ κατενάρκησα ὑμῶν; Χαρίσασθέ μοι τὴν ἀδικίαν ταύτην.

Douay-Rheims

For what is there that you have had less than the other churches, but that I myself was not burthensome to you? Pardon me this injury.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Quid est enim, quod minus habuistis præ ceteris ecclesiis, nisi quod ego ipse non gravavi vos? donate mihi hanc injuriam.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّهُ مَا هُوَ ٱلَّذِي نَقَصْتُمْ عَنْ سَائِرِ ٱلْكَنَائِسِ، إِلَّا أَنِّي أَنَا لَمْ أُثَقِّلْ عَلَيْكُمْ؟ سَامِحُونِي بِهَذَا ٱلظُّلْمِ!

↩

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 12:14.

Behold, the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be burdensome to you: for I seek not yours, but you: for the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἰδού, τρίτον ἑτοίμως ἔχω ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ οὐ καταναρκήσω ὑμῶν· οὐ γὰρ ζητῶ τὰ ὑμῶν, ἀλλὰ ὑμᾶς· οὐ γὰρ ὀφείλει τὰ τέκνα τοῖς γονεῦσιν θησαυρίζειν, ἀλλ’ οἱ γονεῖς τοῖς τέκνοις.

Douay-Rheims

Behold now the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be burthensome unto you. For I seek not the things that are yours, but you. For neither ought the children to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Ecce tertio hoc paratus sum venire ad vos: et non ero gravis vobis. Non enim quæro quæ vestra sunt, sed vos. Nec enim debent filii parentibus thesaurizare, sed parentes filiis.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

هُوَذَا ٱلْمَرَّةُ ٱلثَّالِثَةُ أَنَا مُسْتَعِدٌّ أَنْ آتِيَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَلَا أُثَقِّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ. لِأَنِّي لَسْتُ أَطْلُبُ مَا هُوَ لَكُمْ بَلْ إِيَّاكُمْ. لِأَنَّهُ لَا يَنْبَغِي أَنَّ ٱلْأَوْلَادَ يَذْخَرُونَ لِلْوَالِدِينَ، بَلِ ٱلْوَالِدُونَ لِلْأَوْلَادِ.

↩

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 12:15.

And I will very gladly spend and be spent for you; though the more abundantly I love you, the less I be loved.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἐγὼ δὲ ἥδιστα δαπανήσω καὶ ἐκδαπανηθήσομαι ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν, εἰ καὶ περισσοτέρως ὑμᾶς ἀγαπῶν, ἧττον ἀγαπῶμαι.

Douay-Rheims

But I most gladly will spend and be spent myself for your souls; although loving you more, I be loved less.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Ego autem libentissime impendam, et super impendar ipse pro animabus vestris: licet plus vos diligens, minus diligar.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَأَمَّا أَنَا فَبِكُلِّ سُرُورٍ أُنْفِقُ وَأُنْفَقُ لِأَجْلِ أَنْفُسِكُمْ، وَإِنْ كُنْتُ كُلَّمَا أُحِبُّكُمْ أَكْثَرَ أُحَبُّ أَقَلَّ!

↩

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 12:16.

But be it so, I did not burden you: nevertheless, being crafty, I caught you with guile.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἔστω δέ, ἐγὼ οὐ κατεβάρησα ὑμᾶς· ἀλλ’ ὑπάρχων πανοῦργος, δόλῳ ὑμᾶς ἔλαβον.

Douay-Rheims

But be it so: I did not burthen you: but being crafty, I caught you by guile.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Sed esto: ego vos non gravavi: sed cum essem astutus, dolo vos cepi.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

فَلْيَكُنْ. أَنَا لَمْ أُثَقِّلْ عَلَيْكُمْ، لَكِنْ إِذْ كُنْتُ مُحْتَالًا أَخَذْتُكُمْ بِمَكْرٍ!

↩

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 12:17.

Did I make a gain of you by any of them whom I sent unto you?

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Μή τινα ὧν ἀπέσταλκα πρὸς ὑμᾶς, δι’ αὐτοῦ ἐπλεονέκτησα ὑμᾶς;

Douay-Rheims

Did I overreach you by any of them whom I sent to you?

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Numquid per aliquem eorum, quod misi ad vos, circumveni vos?

Arabic (Van Dyck)

هَلْ طَمِعْتُ فِيكُمْ بِأَحَدٍ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَرْسَلْتُهُمْ إِلَيْكُمْ؟

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 12:18.

I desired Titus, and with [him] I sent a brother. Did Titus make a gain of you? walked we not in the same spirit? [walked we] not in the same steps?

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Παρεκάλεσα Τίτον, καὶ συναπέστειλα τὸν ἀδελφόν· μήτι ἐπλεονέκτησεν ὑμᾶς Τίτος; Οὐ τῷ αὐτῷ πνεύματι περιεπατήσαμεν; Οὐ τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἴχνεσιν;

Douay-Rheims

I desired Titus, and I sent with him a brother. Did Titus overreach you? Did we not walk with the same spirit? did we not in the same steps?

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Rogavi Titum, et misi cum illo fratrem. Numquid Titus vos circumvenit? nonne eodem spiritu ambulavimus? nonne iisdem vestigiis?

Arabic (Van Dyck)

طَلَبْتُ إِلَى تِيطُسَ وَأَرْسَلْتُ مَعَهُ ٱلْأَخَ. هَلْ طَمِعَ فِيكُمْ تِيطُسُ؟ أَمَا سَلَكْنَا بِذَاتِ ٱلرُّوحِ ٱلْوَاحِدِ؟ أَمَا بِذَاتِ ٱلْخَطَوَاتِ ٱلْوَاحِدَةِ؟

Again, think ye that we excuse ourselves unto you? we speak before God in Christ: but [we do] all things, dearly beloved, for your edifying.

Πάλιν δοκεῖτε ὅτι ὑμῖν ἀπολογούμεθα; Κατενώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν χριστῷ λαλοῦμεν· τὰ δὲ πάντα, ἀγαπητοί, ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑμῶν οἰκοδομῆς.

Douay-Rheims

Of old, think you that we excuse ourselves to you? We speak before God in Christ; but all things, my dearly beloved, for your edification.

أَتَظُنُّونَ أَيْضًا أَنَّنَا نَحْتَجُّ لَكُمْ؟ أَمَامَ ٱللهِ فِي ٱلْمَسِيحِ نَتَكَلَّمُ. وَلَكِنَّ ٱلْكُلَّ أَيُّهَا ٱلْأَحِبَّاءُ لِأَجْلِ بُنْيَانِكُمْ.

↩

Paul’s Second Letter to the Corinthians 12:20.

For I fear, lest, when I come, I shall not find you such as I would, and [that] I shall be found unto you such as ye would not: lest [there be] debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults:

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Φοβοῦμαι γάρ, μήπως ἐλθὼν οὐχ οἵους θέλω εὕρω ὑμᾶς, κἀγὼ εὑρεθῶ ὑμῖν οἷον οὐ θέλετε· μήπως ἔρεις, ζῆλοι, θυμοί, ἐριθεῖαι, καταλαλιαί, ψιθυρισμοί, φυσιώσεις, ἀκαταστασίαι·

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Timeo enim ne forte cum venero, non quales volo, inveniam vos: et ego inveniar a vobis, qualem non vultis: ne forte contentiones, æmulationes, animositates, dissensiones, detractiones, susurrationes, inflationes, seditiones sint inter vos:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنِّي أَخَافُ إِذَا جِئْتُ أَنْ لَا أَجِدَكُمْ كَمَا أُرِيدُ، وَأُوجَدَ مِنْكُمْ كَمَا لَا تُرِيدُونَ. أَنْ تُوجَدَ خُصُومَاتٌ وَمُحَاسَدَاتٌ وَسَخَطَاتٌ وَتَحَزُّبَاتٌ وَمَذَمَّاتٌ وَنَمِيمَاتٌ وَتَكَبُّرَاتٌ وَتَشْوِيشَاتٌ.

↩

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

μὴ πάλιν ἐλθόντα με ταπεινώσει ὁ θεός μου πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ πενθήσω πολλοὺς τῶν προημαρτηκότων, καὶ μὴ μετανοησάντων ἐπὶ τῇ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ καὶ πορνείᾳ καὶ ἀσελγείᾳ ᾗ ἔπραξαν.

Douay-Rheims

ne iterum cum venero, humiliet me Deus apud vos, et lugeam multos ex iis qui ante peccaverunt, et non egerunt pœnitentiam super immunditia, et fornicatione, et impudicitia, quam gesserunt.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

أَنْ يُذِلَّنِي إِلَهِي عِنْدَكُمْ، إِذَا جِئْتُ أَيْضًا وَأَنُوحُ عَلَى كَثِيرِينَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَخْطَأُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَمْ يَتُوبُوا عَنِ ٱلنَّجَاسَةِ وَٱلزِّنَا وَٱلْعَهَارَةِ ٱلَّتِي فَعَلُوهَا.

Behold, this is the third time I am coming to you: In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word stand.

Ecce tertio hoc venio ad vos: in ore duorum vel trium testium stabit omne verbum.

Douay-Rheims

Arabic (Van Dyck)

قَدْ سَبَقْتُ فَقُلْتُ، وَأَسْبِقُ فَأَقُولُ كَمَا وَأَنَا حَاضِرٌ ٱلْمَرَّةَ ٱلثَّانِيَةَ، وَأَنَا غَائِبٌ ٱلْآنَ، أَكْتُبُ لِلَّذِينَ أَخْطَأُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ، وَلِجَمِيعِ ٱلْبَاقِينَ: أَنِّي إِذَا جِئْتُ أَيْضًا لَا أُشْفِقُ.

Douay-Rheims

Arabic (Van Dyck)

إِذْ أَنْتُمْ تَطْلُبُونَ بُرْهَانَ ٱلْمَسِيحِ ٱلْمُتَكَلِّمِ فِيَّ، ٱلَّذِي لَيْسَ ضَعِيفًا لَكُمْ بَلْ قَوِيٌّ فِيكُمْ.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

جَرِّبُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ، هَلْ أَنْتُمْ فِي ٱلْإِيمَانِ؟ ٱمْتَحِنُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ. أَمْ لَسْتُمْ تَعْرِفُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ، أَنَّ يَسُوعَ ٱلْمَسِيحَ هُوَ فِيكُمْ، إِنْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا مَرْفُوضِينَ؟

But I trust that ye shall know that we are not reprobates.

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Καὶ συνυπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ Ἰουδαῖοι, ὥστε καὶ Βαρνάβας συναπήχθη αὐτῶν τῇ ὑποκρίσει.

Douay-Rheims

And to his dissimulation the rest of the Jews consented, so that Barnabas also was led by them into that dissimulation.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Et simulationi ejus consenserunt ceteri Judæi, ita ut et Barnabas duceretur ab eis in illam simulationem.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَرَاءَى مَعَهُ بَاقِي ٱلْيَهُودِ أَيْضًا، حَتَّى إِنَّ بَرْنَابَا أَيْضًا ٱنْقَادَ إِلَى رِيَائِهِمْ!

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Galatians 2:14.

But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before [them] all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἀλλ’ ὅτε εἶδον ὅτι οὐκ ὀρθοποδοῦσιν πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, εἶπον τῷ Πέτρῳ ἔμπροσθεν πάντων, Εἰ σύ, Ἰουδαῖος ὑπάρχων, ἐθνικῶς ζῇς καὶ οὐκ Ἰουδαϊκῶς, τί τὰ ἔθνη ἀναγκάζεις Ἰουδαΐζειν;

Douay-Rheims

But when I saw that they walked not uprightly unto the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas before them all: If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of the Gentiles, and not as the Jews do, how dost thou compel the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Sed cum vidissem quod non recte ambularent ad veritatem Evangelii, dixi Cephæ coram omnibus: Si tu, cum Judæus sis, gentiliter vivis, et non judaice: quomodo gentes cogis judaizare?

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لَكِنْ لَمَّا رَأَيْتُ أَنَّهُمْ لَا يَسْلُكُونَ بِٱسْتِقَامَةٍ حَسَبَ حَقِّ ٱلْإِنْجِيلِ، قُلْتُ لِبُطْرُسَ قُدَّامَ ٱلْجَمِيعِ: «إِنْ كُنْتَ وَأَنْتَ يَهُودِيٌّ تَعِيشُ أُمَمِيًّا لَا يَهُودِيًّا، فَلِمَاذَا تُلْزِمُ ٱلْأُمَمَ أَنْ يَتَهَوَّدُوا؟»

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Galatians 2:15.

We [who are] Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἡμεῖς φύσει Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἐθνῶν ἁμαρτωλοί,

Douay-Rheims

We by nature are Jews, and not of the Gentiles sinners.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Nos natura Judæi, et non ex gentibus peccatores.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

نَحْنُ بِٱلطَّبِيعَةِ يَهُودٌ وَلَسْنَا مِنَ ٱلْأُمَمِ خُطَاةً،

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Galatians 2:16.

Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

εἰδότες ὅτι οὐ δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ἔργων νόμου, ἐὰν μὴ διὰ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ, καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐπιστεύσαμεν, ἵνα δικαιωθῶμεν ἐκ πίστεως χριστοῦ, καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων νόμου· διότι οὐ δικαιωθήσεται ἐξ ἔργων νόμου πᾶσα σάρξ.

Douay-Rheims

But knowing that man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ; we also believe in Christ Jesus, that we may be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: because by the works of the law no flesh shall be justified.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Scientes autem quod non justificatur homo ex operibus legis, nisi per fidem Jesu Christi: et nos in Christo Jesu credimus, ut justificemur ex fide Christi, et non ex operibus legis: propter quod ex operibus legis non justificabitur omnis caro.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

إِذْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّ ٱلْإِنْسَانَ لَا يَتَبَرَّرُ بِأَعْمَالِ ٱلنَّامُوسِ، بَلْ بِإِيمَانِ يَسُوعَ ٱلْمَسِيحِ، آمَنَّا نَحْنُ أَيْضًا بِيَسُوعَ ٱلْمَسِيحِ، لِنَتَبَرَّرَ بِإِيمَانِ يَسُوعَ لَا بِأَعْمَالِ ٱلنَّامُوسِ. لِأَنَّهُ بِأَعْمَالِ ٱلنَّامُوسِ لَا يَتَبَرَّرُ جَسَدٌ مَا.

↩

But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, [is] therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Εἰ δέ, ζητοῦντες δικαιωθῆναι ἐν χριστῷ, εὑρέθημεν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἁμαρτωλοί, ἆρα χριστὸς ἁμαρτίας διάκονος; Μὴ γένοιτο.

Douay-Rheims

But if while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners; is Christ then the minister of sin? God forbid.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Quod si quærentes justificari in Christo, inventi sumus et ipsi peccatores, numquid Christus peccati minister est? Absit.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

فَإِنْ كُنَّا وَنَحْنُ طَالِبُونَ أَنْ نَتَبَرَّرَ فِي ٱلْمَسِيحِ، نُوجَدُ نَحْنُ أَنْفُسُنَا أَيْضًا خُطَاةً، أَفَٱلْمَسِيحُ خَادِمٌ لِلْخَطِيَّةِ؟ حَاشَا!

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Galatians 2:18.

For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Εἰ γὰρ ἃ κατέλυσα, ταῦτα πάλιν οἰκοδομῶ, παραβάτην ἐμαυτὸν συνίστημι.

Douay-Rheims

For if I build up again the things which I have destroyed, I make myself a prevaricator.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Si enim quæ destruxi, iterum hæc ædifico: prævaricatorem me constituo.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

فَإِنِّي إِنْ كُنْتُ أَبْنِي أَيْضًا هَذَا ٱلَّذِي قَدْ هَدَمْتُهُ، فَإِنِّي أُظْهِرُ نَفْسِي مُتَعَدِّيًا.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Galatians 2:19.

For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God.

Ἐγὼ γὰρ διὰ νόμου νόμῳ ἀπέθανον, ἵνα θεῷ ζήσω.

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Ego enim per legem, legi mortuus sum, ut Deo vivam: Christo confixus sum cruci.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنِّي مُتُّ بِٱلنَّامُوسِ لِلنَّامُوسِ لِأَحْيَا لِلهِ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Galatians 2:20.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Χριστῷ συνεσταύρωμαι· ζῶ δέ, οὐκέτι ἐγώ, ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ χριστός· ὃ δὲ νῦν ζῶ ἐν σαρκί, ἐν πίστει ζῶ τῇ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντός με καὶ παραδόντος ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

مَعَ ٱلْمَسِيحِ صُلِبْتُ، فَأَحْيَا لَا أَنَا، بَلِ ٱلْمَسِيحُ يَحْيَا فِيَّ. فَمَا أَحْيَاهُ ٱلْآنَ فِي ٱلْجَسَدِ، فَإِنَّمَا أَحْيَاهُ فِي ٱلْإِيمَانِ، إِيمَانِ ٱبْنِ ٱللهِ، ٱلَّذِي أَحَبَّنِي وَأَسْلَمَ نَفْسَهُ لِأَجْلِي.

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 2:6.

Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God:

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

ὃς ἐν μορφῇ θεοῦ ὑπάρχων, οὐχ ἁρπαγμὸν ἡγήσατο τὸ εἶναι ἶσα θεῷ,

Douay-Rheims

Who being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God:

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

qui cum in forma Dei esset, non rapinam arbitratus est esse se æqualem Deo:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

ٱلَّذِي إِذْ كَانَ فِي صُورَةِ ٱللهِ، لَمْ يَحْسِبْ خُلْسَةً أَنْ يَكُونَ مُعَادِلًا لِلهِ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 2:7.

But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 2:8.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

καὶ σχήματι εὑρεθεὶς ὡς ἄνθρωπος, ἐταπείνωσεν ἑαυτόν, γενόμενος ὑπήκοος μέχρι θανάτου, θανάτου δὲ σταυροῦ.

Douay-Rheims

Arabic (Van Dyck)

↩

Douay-Rheims

For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names:

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِذَلِكَ رَفَّعَهُ ٱللهُ أَيْضًا، وَأَعْطَاهُ ٱسْمًا فَوْقَ كُلِّ ٱسْمٍ،

↩

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Douay-Rheims

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِكَيْ تَجْثُوَ بِٱسْمِ يَسُوعَ كُلُّ رُكْبَةٍ مِمَّنْ فِي ٱلسَّمَاءِ، وَمَنْ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ، وَمَنْ تَحْتَ ٱلْأَرْضِ،

↩

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَيَعْتَرِفَ كُلُّ لِسَانٍ أَنَّ يَسُوعَ ٱلْمَسِيحَ هُوَ رَبٌّ، لِمَجْدِ ٱللهِ ٱلْآبِ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 2:12.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ὥστε, ἀγαπητοί μου, καθὼς πάντοτε ὑπηκούσατε, μὴ ὡς ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ μου μόνον, ἀλλὰ νῦν πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἐν τῇ ἀπουσίᾳ μου, μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου τὴν ἑαυτῶν σωτηρίαν κατεργάζεσθε·

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Itaque carissimi mei (sicut semper obedistis), non ut in præsentia mei tantum, sed multo magis nunc in absentia mea, cum metu et tremore vestram salutem operamini.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

إِذًا يَا أَحِبَّائِي، كَمَا أَطَعْتُمْ كُلَّ حِينٍ، لَيْسَ كَمَا فِي حُضُورِي فَقَطْ، بَلِ ٱلْآنَ بِٱلْأَوْلَى جِدًّا فِي غِيَابِي، تَمِّمُوا خَلَاصَكُمْ بِخَوْفٍ وَرِعْدَةٍ،

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 2:13.

For it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of [his] good pleasure.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّ ٱللهَ هُوَ ٱلْعَامِلُ فِيكُمْ أَنْ تُرِيدُوا وَأَنْ تَعْمَلُوا مِنْ أَجْلِ ٱلْمَسَرَّةِ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 2:14.

Do all things without murmurings and disputings:

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Omnia autem facite sine murmurationibus et hæsitationibus:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

اِفْعَلُوا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ بِلَا دَمْدَمَةٍ وَلَا مُجَادَلَةٍ،

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 2:15.

That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world;

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

ἵνα γένησθε ἄμεμπτοι καὶ ἀκέραιοι, τέκνα θεοῦ ἀμώμητα ἐν μέσῳ γενεᾶς σκολιᾶς καὶ διεστραμμένης, ἐν οἷς φαίνεσθε ὡς φωστῆρες ἐν κόσμῳ,

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 3:21.

Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body, according to the working whereby he is able even to subdue all things unto himself.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

ὃς μετασχηματίσει τὸ σῶμα τῆς ταπεινώσεως ἡμῶν, εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸ σύμμορφον τῷ σώματι τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ, κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν τοῦ δύνασθαι αὐτὸν καὶ ὑποτάξαι ἑαυτῷ τὰ πάντα.

Douay-Rheims

Who will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of his glory, according to the operation whereby also he is able to subdue all things unto himself.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

qui reformabit corpus humilitatis nostræ, configuratum corpori claritatis suæ, secundum operationem, qua etiam possit subjicere sibi omnia.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

ٱلَّذِي سَيُغَيِّرُ شَكْلَ جَسَدِ تَوَاضُعِنَا لِيَكُونَ عَلَى صُورَةِ جَسَدِ مَجْدِهِ، بِحَسَبِ عَمَلِ ٱسْتِطَاعَتِهِ أَنْ يُخْضِعَ لِنَفْسِهِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:1.

Therefore, my brethren dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, so stand fast in the Lord, [my] dearly beloved.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοὶ καὶ ἐπιπόθητοι, χαρὰ καὶ στέφανός μου, οὕτως στήκετε ἐν κυρίῳ, ἀγαπητοί.

Douay-Rheims

Therefore, my dearly beloved brethren, and most desired, my joy and my crown; so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Itaque fratres mei carissimi, et desideratissimi, gaudium meum, et corona mea: sic state in Domino, carissimi.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

إِذًا يَا إِخْوَتِي ٱلْأَحِبَّاءَ، وَٱلْمُشْتَاقَ إِلَيْهِمْ، يَا سُرُورِي وَإِكْلِيلِي، ٱثْبُتُوا هَكَذَا فِي ٱلرَّبِّ أَيُّهَا ٱلْأَحِبَّاءُ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:2.

I beseech Euodias, and beseech Syntyche, that they be of the same mind in the Lord.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Εὐοδίαν παρακαλῶ, καὶ Συντύχην παρακαλῶ, τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν ἐν κυρίῳ.

Douay-Rheims

I beg of Evodia, and I beseech Syntyche, to be of one mind in the Lord.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Evodiam rogo, et Syntychen deprecor, idipsum sapere in Domino.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

أَطْلُبُ إِلَى أَفُودِيَةَ وَأَطْلُبُ إِلَى سِنْتِيخِي أَنْ تَفْتَكِرَا فِكْرًا وَاحِدًا فِي ٱلرَّبِّ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:3.

And I intreat thee also, true yokefellow, help those women which laboured with me in the gospel, with Clement also, and [with] other my fellowlabourers, whose names [are] in the book of life.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ναί, ἐρωτῶ καί σε, σύζυγε γνήσιε, συλλαμβάνου αὐταῖς, αἵτινες ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ συνήθλησάν μοι, μετὰ καὶ Κλήμεντος, καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν συνεργῶν μου, ὧν τὰ ὀνόματα ἐν βίβλῳ ζωῆς.

Douay-Rheims

And I entreat thee also, my sincere companion, help those women who have laboured with me in the gospel, with Clement and the rest of my fellow labourers, whose names are in the book of life.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Etiam rogo et te, germane compar, adjuva illas, quæ mecum laboraverunt in Evangelio cum Clemente, et ceteris adjutoribus meis, quorum nomina sunt in libro vitæ.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

نَعَمْ أَسْأَلُكَ أَنْتَ أَيْضًا، يَا شَرِيكِي ٱلْمُخْلِصَ، سَاعِدْ هَاتَيْنِ ٱللَّتَيْنِ جَاهَدَتَا مَعِي فِي ٱلْإِنْجِيلِ، مَعَ أَكْلِيمَنْدُسَ أَيْضًا وَبَاقِي ٱلْعَامِلِينَ مَعِي، ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْمَاؤُهُمْ فِي سِفْرِ ٱلْحَيَاةِ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:4.

Rejoice in the Lord alway: [and] again I say, Rejoice.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Χαίρετε ἐν κυρίῳ πάντοτε· πάλιν ἐρῶ, χαίρετε.

Douay-Rheims

Rejoice in the Lord always; again, I say, rejoice.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Gaudete in Domino semper: iterum dico gaudete.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

اِفْرَحُوا فِي ٱلرَّبِّ كُلَّ حِينٍ، وَأَقُولُ أَيْضًا: ٱفْرَحُوا.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:5.

Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord [is] at hand.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Τὸ ἐπιεικὲς ὑμῶν γνωσθήτω πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις. Ὁ κύριος ἐγγύς.

Douay-Rheims

Let your modesty be known to all men. The Lord is nigh.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Modestia vestra nota sit omnibus hominibus: Dominus prope est.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِيَكُنْ حِلْمُكُمْ مَعْرُوفًا عِنْدَ جَمِيعِ ٱلنَّاسِ. اَلرَّبُّ قَرِيبٌ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:6.

Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Μηδὲν μεριμνᾶτε, ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ τῇ δεήσει μετὰ εὐχαριστίας τὰ αἰτήματα ὑμῶν γνωριζέσθω πρὸς τὸν θεόν.

Douay-Rheims

Be nothing solicitous; but in every thing, by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known to God.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Nihil solliciti sitis: sed in omni oratione, et obsecratione, cum gratiarum actione petitiones vestræ innotescant apud Deum.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لَا تَهْتَمُّوا بِشَيْءٍ، بَلْ فِي كُلِّ شَيْءٍ بِٱلصَّلَاةِ وَٱلدُّعَاءِ مَعَ ٱلشُّكْرِ، لِتُعْلَمْ طِلْبَاتُكُمْ لَدَى ٱللهِ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:7.

And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Καὶ ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ ὑπερέχουσα πάντα νοῦν, φρουρήσει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν καὶ τὰ νοήματα ὑμῶν ἐν χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

Douay-Rheims

And the peace of God, which surpasseth all understanding, keep your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Et pax Dei, quæ exuperat omnem sensum, custodiat corda vestra, et intelligentias vestras in Christo Jesu.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَسَلَامُ ٱللهِ ٱلَّذِي يَفُوقُ كُلَّ عَقْلٍ، يَحْفَظُ قُلُوبَكُمْ وَأَفْكَارَكُمْ فِي ٱلْمَسِيحِ يَسُوعَ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:8.

Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things [are] honest, whatsoever things [are] just, whatsoever things [are] pure, whatsoever things [are] lovely, whatsoever things [are] of good report; if [there be] any virtue, and if [there be] any praise, think on these things.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Τὸ λοιπόν, ἀδελφοί, ὅσα ἐστὶν ἀληθῆ, ὅσα σεμνά, ὅσα δίκαια, ὅσα ἁγνά, ὅσα προσφιλῆ, ὅσα εὔφημα, εἴ τις ἀρετὴ καὶ εἴ τις ἔπαινος, ταῦτα λογίζεσθε.

Douay-Rheims

For the rest, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever modest, whatsoever just, whatsoever holy, whatsoever lovely, whatsoever of good fame, if there be any virtue, if any praise of discipline, think on these things.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

De cetero fratres, quæcumque sunt vera, quæcumque pudica, quæcumque justa, quæcumque sancta, quæcumque amabilia, quæcumque bonæ famæ, siqua virtus, siqua laus disciplinæ, hæc cogitate.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

أَخِيرًا أَيُّهَا ٱلْإِخْوَةُ، كُلُّ مَا هُوَ حَقٌّ، كُلُّ مَا هُوَ جَلِيلٌ، كُلُّ مَا هُوَ عَادِلٌ، كُلُّ مَا هُوَ طَاهِرٌ، كُلُّ مَا هُوَ مُسِرٌّ، كُلُّ مَا صِيتُهُ حَسَنٌ، إِنْ كَانَتْ فَضِيلَةٌ وَإِنْ كَانَ مَدْحٌ، فَفِي هَذِهِ ٱفْتَكِرُوا.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:9.

Those things, which ye have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, do: and the God of peace shall be with you.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἃ καὶ ἐμάθετε καὶ παρελάβετε καὶ ἠκούσατε καὶ εἴδετε ἐν ἐμοί, ταῦτα πράσσετε· καὶ ὁ θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης ἔσται μεθ’ ὑμῶν.

Douay-Rheims

The things which you have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, these do ye, and the God of peace shall be with you.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Quæ et didicistis, et accepistis, et audistis, et vidistis in me, hæc agite: et Deus pacis erit vobiscum.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَمَا تَعَلَّمْتُمُوهُ، وَتَسَلَّمْتُمُوهُ، وَسَمِعْتُمُوهُ، وَرَأَيْتُمُوهُ فِيَّ، فَهَذَا ٱفْعَلُوا، وَإِلَهُ ٱلسَّلَامِ يَكُونُ مَعَكُمْ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:10.

But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly, that now at the last your care of me hath flourished again; wherein ye were also careful, but ye lacked opportunity.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἐχάρην δὲ ἐν κυρίῳ μεγάλως, ὅτι ἤδη ποτὲ ἀνεθάλετε τὸ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ φρονεῖν· ἐφ’ ᾧ καὶ ἐφρονεῖτε, ἠκαιρεῖσθε δέ.

Douay-Rheims

Now I rejoice in the Lord exceedingly, that now at length your thought for me hath flourished again, as you did also think; but you were busied.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Gavisus sum autem in Domino vehementer, quoniam tandem aliquando refloruistis pro me sentire, sicut et sentiebatis: occupati autem eratis.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

ثُمَّ إِنِّي فَرِحْتُ بِٱلرَّبِّ جِدًّا لِأَنَّكُمُ ٱلْآنَ قَدْ أَزْهَرَ أَيْضًا مَرَّةً ٱعْتِنَاؤُكُمْ بِي ٱلَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تَعْتَنُونَهُ، وَلَكِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ لَكُمْ فُرْصَةٌ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:11.

Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, [therewith] to be content.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Οὐχ ὅτι καθ’ ὑστέρησιν λέγω· ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔμαθον, ἐν οἷς εἰμί, αὐτάρκης εἶναι.

Douay-Rheims

I speak not as it were for want. For I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, to be content therewith.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Non quasi propter penuriam dico: ego enim didici, in quibus sum, sufficiens esse.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لَيْسَ أَنِّي أَقُولُ مِنْ جِهَةِ ٱحْتِيَاجٍ، فَإِنِّي قَدْ تَعَلَّمْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مُكْتَفِيًا بِمَا أَنَا فِيهِ.

↩

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:12.

I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Οἶδα καὶ ταπεινοῦσθαι, οἶδα καὶ περισσεύειν· ἐν παντὶ καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν μεμύημαι καὶ χορτάζεσθαι καὶ πεινᾷν, καὶ περισσεύειν καὶ ὑστερεῖσθαι.

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Scio et humiliari, scio et abundare (ubique et in omnibus institutus sum): et satiari, et esurire, et abundare, et penuriam pati.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

أَعْرِفُ أَنْ أَتَّضِعَ وَأَعْرِفُ أَيْضًا أَنْ أَسْتَفْضِلَ. فِي كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَفِي جَمِيعِ ٱلْأَشْيَاءِ قَدْ تَدَرَّبْتُ أَنْ أَشْبَعَ وَأَنْ أَجُوعَ، وَأَنْ أَسْتَفْضِلَ وَأَنْ أَنْقُصَ.

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:13.

I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:14.

Douay-Rheims

Arabic (Van Dyck)

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:15.

Now ye Philippians know also, that in the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church communicated with me as concerning giving and receiving, but ye only.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Οἴδατε δὲ καὶ ὑμεῖς, Φιλιππήσιοι, ὅτι ἐν ἀρχῇ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, ὅτε ἐξῆλθον ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας, οὐδεμία μοι ἐκκλησία ἐκοινώνησεν εἰς λόγον δόσεως καὶ λήψεως, εἰ μὴ ὑμεῖς μόνοι·

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَأَنْتُمْ أَيْضًا تَعْلَمُونَ أَيُّهَا ٱلْفِيلِبِّيُّونَ أَنَّهُ فِي بَدَاءَةِ ٱلْإِنْجِيلِ،لَمَّا خَرَجْتُ مِنْ مَكِدُونِيَّةَ، لَمْ تُشَارِكْنِي كَنِيسَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فِي حِسَابِ ٱلْعَطَاءِ وَٱلْأَخْذِ إِلَّا أَنْتُمْ وَحْدَكُمْ.

Not because I desire a gift: but I desire fruit that may abound to your account.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.

Paul’s Letter to the Philippians 4:21.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

et Jesus, qui dicitur Justus: qui sunt ex circumcisione: hi soli sunt adjutores mei in regno Dei, qui mihi fuerunt solatio.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

Douay-Rheims

And to wait for his Son from heaven (whom he raised up from the dead,) Jesus, who hath delivered us from the wrath to come.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

et exspectare Filium ejus de cælis (quem suscitavit a mortuis) Jesum, qui eripuit nos ab ira ventura.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَتَنْتَظِرُوا ٱبْنَهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَاءِ، ٱلَّذِي أَقَامَهُ مِنَ ٱلْأَمْوَاتِ، يَسُوعَ، ٱلَّذِي يُنْقِذُنَا مِنَ ٱلْغَضَبِ ٱلْآتِي.

↩

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:1.

For yourselves, brethren, know our entrance in unto you, that it was not in vain:

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Αὐτοὶ γὰρ οἴδατε, ἀδελφοί, τὴν εἴσοδον ἡμῶν τὴν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ὅτι οὐ κενὴ γέγονεν·

Douay-Rheims

For yourselves know, brethren, our entrance in unto you, that it was not in vain:

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Nam ipsi scitis, fratres, introitum nostrum ad vos, quia non inanis fuit:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّكُمْ أَنْتُمْ أَيُّهَا ٱلْإِخْوَةُ تَعْلَمُونَ دُخُولَنَا إِلَيْكُمْ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ بَاطِلًا،

↩

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:2.

But even after that we had suffered before, and were shamefully entreated, as ye know, at Philippi, we were bold in our God to speak unto you the gospel of God with much contention.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

ἀλλὰ προπαθόντες καὶ ὑβρισθέντες, καθὼς οἴδατε, ἐν Φιλίπποις, ἐπαρρησιασάμεθα ἐν τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν λαλῆσαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν πολλῷ ἀγῶνι.

Douay-Rheims

But having suffered many things before, and been shamefully treated (as you know) at Philippi, we had confidence in our God, to speak unto you the gospel of God in much carefulness.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

sed ante passi, et contumeliis affecti (sicut scitis) in Philippis, fiduciam habuimus in Deo nostro, loqui ad vos Evangelium Dei in multa sollicitudine.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بَلْ بَعْدَ مَا تَأَلَّمْنَا قَبْلًا وَبُغِيَ عَلَيْنَا كَمَا تَعْلَمُونَ، فِي فِيلِبِّي، جَاهَرْنَا فِي إِلَهِنَا أَنْ نُكَلِّمَكُمْ بِإِنْجِيلِ ٱللهِ، فِي جِهَادٍ كَثِيرٍ.

↩

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:3.

For our exhortation [was] not of deceit, nor of uncleanness, nor in guile:

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Ἡ γὰρ παράκλησις ἡμῶν οὐκ ἐκ πλάνης, οὐδὲ ἐξ ἀκαθαρσίας, οὔτε ἐν δόλῳ·

Douay-Rheims

For our exhortation was not of error, nor of uncleanness, nor in deceit:

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Exhortatio enim nostra non de errore, neque de immunditia, neque in dolo,

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّ وَعْظَنَا لَيْسَ عَنْ ضَلَالٍ، وَلَا عَنْ دَنَسٍ، وَلَا بِمَكْرٍ،

↩

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:4.

But as we were allowed of God to be put in trust with the gospel, even so we speak; not as pleasing men, but God, which trieth our hearts.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

ἀλλὰ καθὼς δεδοκιμάσμεθα ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ πιστευθῆναι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, οὕτως λαλοῦμεν, οὐχ ὡς ἀνθρώποις ἀρέσκοντες, ἀλλὰ τῷ θεῷ τῷ δοκιμάζοντι τὰς καρδίας ἡμῶν.

Douay-Rheims

But as we were approved by God that the gospel should be committed to us: even so we speak, not as pleasing men, but God, who proveth our hearts.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

sed sicut probati sumus a Deo ut crederetur nobis Evangelium: ita loquimur non quasi hominibus placentes, sed Deo, qui probat corda nostra.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بَلْ كَمَا ٱسْتُحْسِنَّا مِنَ ٱللهِ أَنْ نُؤْتَمَنَ عَلَى ٱلْإِنْجِيلِ، هَكَذَا نَتَكَلَّمُ، لَا كَأَنَّنَا نُرْضِي ٱلنَّاسَ بَلِ ٱللهَ ٱلَّذِي يَخْتَبِرُ قُلُوبَنَا.

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:5.

For neither at any time used we flattering words, as ye know, nor a cloke of covetousness; God [is] witness:

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Οὔτε γάρ ποτε ἐν λόγῳ κολακείας ἐγενήθημεν, καθὼς οἴδατε, οὔτε ἐν προφάσει πλεονεξίας· θεὸς μάρτυς·

Douay-Rheims

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Neque enim aliquando fuimus in sermone adulationis, sicut scitis: neque in occasione avaritiæ: Deus testis est:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

فَإِنَّنَا لَمْ نَكُنْ قَطُّ فِي كَلَامِ تَمَلُّقٍ كَمَا تَعْلَمُونَ، وَلَا فِي عِلَّةِ طَمَعٍ. ٱللهُ شَاهِدٌ.

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:6.

Nor of men sought we glory, neither of you, nor [yet] of others, when we might have been burdensome, as the apostles of Christ.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

οὔτε ζητοῦντες ἐξ ἀνθρώπων δόξαν, οὔτε ἀφ’ ὑμῶν οὔτε ἀπὸ ἄλλων, δυνάμενοι ἐν βάρει εἶναι, ὡς χριστοῦ ἀπόστολοι,

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَلَا طَلَبْنَا مَجْدًا مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ، لَا مِنْكُمْ وَلَا مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ، مَعَ أَنَّنَا قَادِرُونَ أَنْ نَكُونَ فِي وَقَارٍ كَرُسُلِ ٱلْمَسِيحِ.

Douay-Rheims

Whereas we might have been burdensome to you, as the apostles of Christ: but we became little ones in the midst of you, as if a nurse should cherish her children:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

بَلْ كُنَّا مُتَرَفِّقِينَ فِي وَسَطِكُمْ كَمَا تُرَبِّي ٱلْمُرْضِعَةُ أَوْلَادَهَا،

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:8.

So being affectionately desirous of you, we were willing to have imparted unto you, not the gospel of God only, but also our own souls, because ye were dear unto us.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

οὕτως, ὁμειρόμενοι ὑμῶν, εὐδοκοῦμεν μεταδοῦναι ὑμῖν οὐ μόνον τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰς ἑαυτῶν ψυχάς, διότι ἀγαπητοὶ ἡμῖν γεγένησθε.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

هَكَذَا إِذْ كُنَّا حَانِّينَ إِلَيْكُمْ، كُنَّا نَرْضَى أَنْ نُعْطِيَكُمْ، لَا إِنْجِيلَ ٱللهِ فَقَطْ بَلْ أَنْفُسَنَا أَيْضًا، لِأَنَّكُمْ صِرْتُمْ مَحْبُوبِينَ إِلَيْنَا.

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:9.

For ye remember, brethren, our labour and travail: for labouring night and day, because we would not be chargeable unto any of you, we preached unto you the gospel of God.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Μνημονεύετε γάρ, ἀδελφοί, τὸν κόπον ἡμῶν καὶ τὸν μόχθον· νυκτὸς γὰρ καὶ ἡμέρας ἐργαζόμενοι, πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἐπιβαρῆσαί τινα ὑμῶν, ἐκηρύξαμεν εἰς ὑμᾶς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 2:13.

For this cause also thank we God without ceasing, because, when ye received the word of God which ye heard of us, ye received [it] not [as] the word of men, but as it is in truth, the word of God, which effectually worketh also in you that believe.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡμεῖς εὐχαριστοῦμεν τῷ θεῷ ἀδιαλείπτως, ὅτι παραλαβόντες λόγον ἀκοῆς παρ’ ἡμῶν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐδέξασθε οὐ λόγον ἀνθρώπων, ἀλλὰ καθώς ἐστιν ἀληθῶς, λόγον θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἐνεργεῖται ἐν ὑμῖν τοῖς πιστεύουσιν.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

For God hath not called us unto uncleanness, but unto holiness.

Douay-Rheims

For God hath not called us unto uncleanness, but unto sanctification.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Non enim vocavit nos Deus in immunditiam, sed in sanctificationem.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّ ٱللهَ لَمْ يَدْعُنَا لِلنَّجَاسَةِ بَلْ فِي ٱلْقَدَاسَةِ.

He therefore that despiseth, despiseth not man, but God, who hath also given unto us his holy Spirit.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Douay-Rheims

Therefore, he that despiseth these things, despiseth not man, but God, who also hath given his holy Spirit in us.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Itaque qui hæc spernit, non hominem spernit, sed Deum: qui etiam dedit Spiritum suum Sanctum in nobis.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

إِذًا مَنْ يُرْذِلُ لَا يُرْذِلُ إِنْسَانًا، بَلِ ٱللهَ ٱلَّذِي أَعْطَانَا أَيْضًا رُوحَهُ ٱلْقُدُّوسَ.

But as touching brotherly love ye need not that I write unto you: for ye yourselves are taught of God to love one another.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Περὶ δὲ τῆς φιλαδελφίας οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε γράφειν ὑμῖν· αὐτοὶ γὰρ ὑμεῖς θεοδίδακτοί ἐστε εἰς τὸ ἀγαπᾷν ἀλλήλους·

Douay-Rheims

But as touching the charity of brotherhood, we have no need to write to you: for yourselves have learned of God to love one another.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

De caritate autem fraternitatis non necesse habemus scribere vobis: ipsi enim vos a Deo didicistis ut diligatis invicem.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَأَمَّا ٱلْمَحَبَّةُ ٱلْأَخَوِيَّةُ فَلَا حَاجَةَ لَكُمْ أَنْ أَكْتُبَ إِلَيْكُمْ عَنْهَا، لِأَنَّكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ مُتَعَلِّمُونَ مِنَ ٱللهِ أَنْ يُحِبَّ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

And that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you;

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

καὶ φιλοτιμεῖσθαι ἡσυχάζειν, καὶ πράσσειν τὰ ἴδια, καὶ ἐργάζεσθαι ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσὶν ὑμῶν, καθὼς ὑμῖν παρηγγείλαμεν·

Douay-Rheims

et opera detis ut quieti sitis, et ut vestrum negotium agatis, et operemini manibus vestris, sicut præcepimus vobis:

Arabic (Van Dyck)

وَأَنْ تَحْرِصُوا عَلَى أَنْ تَكُونُوا هَادِئِينَ، وَتُمَارِسُوا أُمُورَكُمُ ٱلْخَاصَّةَ، وَتَشْتَغِلُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ أَنْتُمْ كَمَا أَوْصَيْنَاكُمْ،

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 4:12.

That ye may walk honestly toward them that are without, and [that] ye may have lack of nothing.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Douay-Rheims

And we will not have you ignorant, brethren, concerning them that are asleep, that you be not sorrowful, even as others who have no hope.

et ut honeste ambuletis ad eos qui foris sunt: et nullius aliquid desideretis.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِكَيْ تَسْلُكُوا بِلِيَاقَةٍ عِنْدَ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ مِنْ خَارِجٍ، وَلَا تَكُونَ لَكُمْ حَاجَةٌ إِلَى أَحَدٍ.

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 4:13.

But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Οὐ θέλομεν δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, περὶ τῶν κεκοιμημένων, ἵνα μὴ λυπῆσθε, καθὼς καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ οἱ μὴ ἔχοντες ἐλπίδα.

Douay-Rheims

For if we believe that Jesus died, and rose again; even so them who have slept through Jesus, will God bring with him.

Latin (Clementine Vulgate)

Nolumus autem vos ignorare fratres de dormientibus, ut non contristemini sicut et ceteri, qui spem non habent.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

ثُمَّ لَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَجْهَلُوا أَيُّهَا ٱلْإِخْوَةُ مِنْ جِهَةِ ٱلرَّاقِدِينَ، لِكَيْ لَا تَحْزَنُوا كَٱلْبَاقِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا رَجَاءَ لَهُمْ.

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 4:14.

For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Εἰ γὰρ πιστεύομεν ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἀπέθανεν καὶ ἀνέστη, οὕτως καὶ ὁ θεὸς τοὺς κοιμηθέντας διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἄξει σὺν αὐτῷ.

Douay-Rheims

For this we say unto you in the word of the Lord, that we who are alive, who remain unto the coming of the Lord, shall not prevent them who have slept.

Arabic (Van Dyck)

لِأَنَّهُ إِنْ كُنَّا نُؤْمِنُ أَنَّ يَسُوعَ مَاتَ وَقَامَ، فَكَذَلِكَ ٱلرَّاقِدُونَ بِيَسُوعَ، سَيُحْضِرُهُمُ ٱللهُ أَيْضًا مَعَهُ.

Paul’s First Letter to the Thessalonians 4:15.

For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we which are alive [and] remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep.

Greek (Byzantine Majority Text)

Τοῦτο γὰρ ὑμῖν λέγομεν ἐν λόγῳ κυρίου, ὅτι ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες οἱ περιλειπόμενοι εἰς τὴν παρουσίαν τοῦ κυρίου, οὐ μὴ φθάσωμεν τοὺς κοιμηθέντας.
